decoded_pov.dedup: __asan_memmove--pcpp::RawPacket::insertData(int, unsigned char const*, unsigned long)--pcpp::Packet::extendLayer(pcpp::Layer*, int, unsigned long)

analyzed_vuln.description: BgpUpdateMessageLayer::setNetworkLayerReachabilityInfo computes an insertion offset from packet fields (withdrawn-routes/path-attributes lengths) and calls extendLayer() without validating that the computed offset is within the current layer bounds. For malformed BGP UPDATE data, this offset can exceed the actual raw packet length, so Packet::extendLayer passes an out-of-range index to RawPacket::insertData. RawPacket::insertData then does memmove(..., m_RawDataLen - atIndex) with atIndex > m_RawDataLen, causing unsigned underflow to a huge size (seen by ASan as negative-size-param).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In FuzzTargetNg, readParsedPacket mutates parsed BGP UPDATE layers and invokes setWithdrawnRoutes/setNetworkLayerReachabilityInfo on attacker-controlled packet contents from the fuzzed input. A crafted packet with inconsistent internal BGP length fields (so computed NLRI start offset is beyond actual packet data) plus a path that triggers NLRI growth (newNlriDataLen > curNlriDataLen, causing extendLayer) leads to extendLayer -> RawPacket::insertData with out-of-bounds insertion index and the crashing memmove size underflow.
